# Point Roberts ocean view

> A three.js model of Point Roberts, Washington, standing on live data. The
> terrain is a NOAA survey, the buildings are OpenStreetMap and hand surveys off
> aerial photographs, and the water, the sky, the ships, the aircraft, the queue
> at the border and the Sheriff's calls are all read from public feeds as they
> happen. Everything you can see the page do can be done by URL, and everything
> the page knows can be read over HTTP.

Point Roberts is a five square mile piece of the United States hanging below the
49th parallel, reachable by road only through Canada. The model covers the whole
peninsula and ten kilometres of the water round it.

## Driving the view

The page is its URL. Where the camera stands and what it points at live in the
hash, and the hash is rewritten as the camera moves, so the address bar is
always the view on the screen. Open a URL with a hash and the camera goes there.

```
https://<host>/#eye=48.999711,-123.068253,158.9&aim=49.001271,-123.068253,53.2&fov=25
```

- `eye=lat,lon,height` — where the camera is. Height is metres above MLLW, the
  same datum as the tide, not above the ground.
- `aim=lat,lon,height` — the point it looks at. A viewpoint, not a vehicle: the
  two together reconstruct as a look-around view however they were captured.
- `fov=degrees` — the vertical field of view. The page's own lens is 25. Values
  outside 5 to 120 are ignored rather than applied.
- `hour=0` to `hour=23.99` — open at that hour of the day, as a decimal. The sun,
  the sky, the tide and the wind all move to it. Left off, the page stands on the
  real clock. Zero means midnight, not "no hour given".
- `map=1` `golf=1` `cast=1` `novel=1` `campground=1` `brademy=1` `pavilion=1` —
  switches, on only. Anything absent is off.

`eye` and `aim` are both required. A hash with one of them and not the other is
ignored entirely, because half a viewpoint is worse than none.

## Named places

You cannot ask for the marina by name in a URL, only by its coordinates. This is
the list of what those coordinates are.

- [/api/places](/api/places): every named thing on the peninsula — the surveyed
  buildings, the OpenStreetMap landmarks, the airstrip, the old cannery wharf —
  each with its position, how wide it is, the ground height under it, and a
  ready-made `hash` that frames it. Append that hash to the site URL and the
  camera is looking at it. `also_called` carries the other names for the same
  ground.

## Reading what it knows

- [/api/state](/api/state): what every feed is saying right now, as one GET. The
  same structure the page receives when it connects.
- [/openapi.json](/openapi.json) and [/docs](/docs): the HTTP surface.
- `ws://<host>/ws/live`: the live feed. A snapshot on connect, then one message
  per reading as it arrives. A browser drawing at sixty frames a second wants
  this; anything asking one question wants `/api/state`.

Every reading is wrapped in an envelope rather than handed over bare:

```json
{ "message_type": "tide.state",
  "source": "tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov",
  "source_time": "2026-09-13T03:06:48+00:00",
  "quality": { "age_seconds": 41.2, "stale": false },
  "data": { "water_level_m": 2.914, "datum": "MLLW", "trend": "falling" } }
```

`source` is who said it, `source_time` is when they took the reading, and
`quality.stale` is whether it is too old to be called the present one. A number
without those attached is not a reading, so nothing here is sent without them.

`provider_health` in the snapshot carries one word per feed: `live`, `offline`,
`scraped` for ships found by scraping rather than by AIS, or `idle` for a feed
nobody is looking at and the server is therefore not polling. A feed that fails
says so; it never shows its last good numbers as current.

## Where the data comes from

| feed | source | what it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| tide | NOAA CO-OPS 9449639 and 9449424 | Point Roberts' own prediction with the surge measured at Cherry Point carried onto it, metres above MLLW |
| currents | NOAA CO-OPS PUG1726 bin 35 | predicted stream 8.1 km offshore, which is the nearest published station |
| weather | Open-Meteo | wind, cloud by layer, haze, and the sea state |
| vessels | AISStream.io | live AIS, with a scraped fallback when it is down |
| aircraft | adsb.fi | community-fed ADS-B, 20 km around the bluff |
| wait | bwt.cbp.gov | the queue at the border now, by lane |
| crossings | data.bts.gov | how many came through the booth, by month, back to 1994 |
| blotter | Whatcom County Sheriff | the daily activity report, one PDF a day |
| golf | pointrobertsgc.com | the club's booking sheet for today |
| marina | pointrobertsmarina.com webcam | vehicles and people counted off the picture |

Tide and weather carry a baked forecast run beside the present reading, so
moving the clock reads the water and the sky at that hour rather than showing
the present one under a different sun. Past the end of the run it says it does
not know. Ships and aircraft are live positions with no archive anywhere, so
they are not shown on a past day at all.

## At the keyboard

`M` mode · `V` fly · `B` boat, again to step ashore · `O` overview · `T` tennis
courts · `G` campground · `F` golf holes · `P` the cast · `R` the novel's route ·
`K` the Sheriff's calls · `H` pavilion · `L` vessel tracks · `C` the photograph ·
`N` next camera · `E` edit camera placement · `S` save camera placement ·
`Esc` drop the selection.

With the Sheriff's calls up, the left and right arrows step to the call before
and the call after, wrapping at both ends, and the card says which one of how
many is on screen. Each step goes to the location and plays the re-enactment.

The clock is a slider and a date box at the foot of the page. The slider moves
the hour twelve either way; the date reaches back as far as the oldest month the
crossing figures cover. Both end up in the hash as `hour=`.

## The code

No bundler and no npm install. The browser loads ES modules straight from `src/`
and three.js from a CDN. The server is FastAPI.

- `src/main.js` — the scene, the modes, and what to re-read when something moves
- `src/config.js` — the origin, the opening view, the datums
- `src/geo.js` — the local east-north-up projection everything is drawn in
- `src/share.js` — reading and writing the hash above
- `src/clock-control.js`, `src/clock.js` — the hour and the day the scene stands at
- `src/feed.js` — the websocket client
- `src/scene/` — one module per thing drawn, and the hand surveys in `*-plan.js`
- `server/proxy.py` — the socket, the clients, the snapshot and one loop per feed
- `server/noaa.py`, `weather.py`, `crossings.py`, `wait.py`, `tee.py`,
  `blotter.py`, `marina.py`, `shipfinder.py` — one module per upstream
- `scripts/build_*.py` — everything under `assets/` is generated by one of these

Tests run without a browser and without a test runner: `node src/test-*.mjs` and
`node src/scene/test-*.mjs`, `python server/test_*.py`. Each prints its own lines
and exits non-zero on a failure.

way it is. That is a working note and is deliberately not served here.
